advances: Original-volume mean identity conditional on supplied mixed contact rows.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The $L$-mean makes $\bar\rho_i$ a probability, and multiplication of the supplied inverse-density decomposition by $L$ proves the mixture. In a row one has $L-L_i=a_i\cdot(w-Y_i)$ almost everywhere by contact. Therefore
$$
\bar Y_i-Y_i
=\frac1{L_i}\int(w-Y_i)(L-L_i)\,d\rho_i
=\frac{C_i a_i}{L_i}.
$$
Contracting with $a_i$ gives the variance identity. Subtracting the equalities for two contact planes gives $(a_i-a'_i)\cdot(w-Y_i)=0$ almost everywhere, hence $C_i(a_i-a'_i)=0$. If the vector displacement is zero then the variance is zero and the $L$-mean is $L_i$. Conversely constant row $L$ makes its two laws identical, hence their means equal. The block and full-centroid formulas follow by projection and the mixture.
statement:
Let $dm$ be finite positive mixed volume of mass $M$ supported on a compact sampled set $S$, and let $L>0$ be continuous on $C=\operatorname{conv}S$. Assume positive weights $\sigma_i$ summing to one and probability laws $\rho_i$ on $S$ satisfy $\int w\,d\rho_i=Y_i$, $\int L\,d\rho_i=L_i=L(Y_i)$ and $\sum_i(\sigma_i/L_i)\rho_i=dm/(ML)$. Suppose for each row there is an affine majorant $A_i\ge L$ on $C$ touching $L$ at $Y_i$ and agreeing with $L$ $\rho_i$-almost everywhere. Let $a_i$ be its full linear part, $C_i=\operatorname{Cov}_{\rho_i}(w)$, and $d\bar\rho_i=(L/L_i)d\rho_i$. Then $\bar\rho_i$ are probabilities with $dm/M=\sum_i\sigma_i\bar\rho_i$, and their means $\bar Y_i$ obey
$$
\bar Y_i-Y_i=C_i a_i/L_i,\qquad
a_i\cdot(\bar Y_i-Y_i)=\operatorname{Var}_{\rho_i}(L)/L_i.
$$
The vector $C_i a_i$ is independent of the choice of touching contact plane. The mean displacement is zero exactly when $L=L_i$ $\rho_i$-almost everywhere, equivalently when $\bar\rho_i=\rho_i$. Writing $a_i=(b_i,c_i)$ in base and continuous coordinates, the continuous displacement is $(C_i^{Xz}b_i+C_i^{XX}c_i)/L_i$. The original mixed centroid is $\sum_i\sigma_i[Y_i+C_i a_i/L_i]$.
title: Exact centroid displacement of an original-volume contact row
